name: Triveni Turbine Ltd
title: Triveni Turbine Ltd - 533655 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 revenue record ₹6.8bn (+26%) but margin compressed on NTPC low-margin order and MTM loss; receivables swelled to ₹6.39bn (84 days vs 49), closing order book +8% to ₹20.54bn.

summary.headline: Triveni Turbine FY26 revenue rose 9% to ₹21.81 bn, a record; Q4 revenue hit ₹6.8 bn (+26%) but PAT fell 3% on a ₹157 mn exceptional charge.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as satisfactory despite geopolitical disruption, US tariff issues and the West Asia conflict, with H2 revenue growing over 125% year-on-year. Q4 posted record quarterly revenue of ₹6.8 bn, with exports at 60% of revenue, but margins compressed on a lower Aftermarket mix, a low-margin strategic NTPC battery-storage order and a mark-to-market loss on the rupee. Q4 order booking rose 19% to ₹7.54 bn, closing order book rose 8% to ₹20.54 bn, and the enquiry book was said to have nearly doubled, led by the US and India. Receivables ballooned to ₹6.39 bn (84 receivable days versus 49), which management expects to unwind, though FY27 is guided to be back-ended again.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY, due to ₹157 mn exceptional charge under new wage code

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Aftermarket was 25% of Q4 sales versus about 33% a year earlier, which weighed on margins; Q4 Aftermarket order booking grew 121% YoY to 50% of order booking. Management expects Aftermarket to contribute more to FY27 revenue in the US.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Exports were 58% of FY26 revenue (up 30% YoY) and 51% of closing order book. FY26 export order inflow was flat YoY at about ₹1,200 crore; management expects FY27 exports to exceed domestic.

segments.name: API (oil & gas)
segments.commentary: Large API orders anticipated in FY26 did not materialise, so API is a lower share of order book than planned, though revenue share is higher. Management expects API to return to 10%+ of order booking and revenue.

segments.name: US subsidiary
segments.commentary: Q4 was profitable for the US subsidiary, but FY26 showed a loss of about ₹8 crore. Management targets positive FY27 or at worst breakeven, with profitability from FY28.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give explicit revenue guidance; it pointed to the 9% closing order book growth as a minimum indicator for FY27 execution.
FY27 expected to be back-ended again; receivables at 31 Mar 2027 may stay near current levels because of the execution profile.
Margins expected to hold around 25%+ EBITDA on a trailing basis, with quarterly volatility; management said there is no structural margin decline.
Management expects order booking growth in FY27, with the US a contributor, though the US enquiry book is not expected to convert quickly due to permitting.
No Middle East API revenue included in projections; management sees a global resurgence in API enquiries due to higher oil prices.
capex_capacity: Enquiry book for steam turbine products is about 18 GW, nearly double FY25; India enquiry about 7 GW (up about 100%); North America about 3 GW.
CO2-based (sCO2) energy storage project for NTPC is being completed; the company will define its business plan after the plant stabilises.
Organic Rankine Cycle turbine being introduced for low-temperature waste heat and geothermal applications.
Over 7.5% of workforce in R&D and 8%+ in engineering; more than 35% in servicing.
Company plans significantly higher investment in AI, without specifying amounts.
demand_pricing: Enquiry growth is broad across steel, cement, process cogeneration, sugar, IPPs and oil and gas; steel and cement hold the largest enquiry base.

US demand is driven by combined-cycle steam turbines for data centres, biomass, pulp and paper, geothermal and some small modular reactor enquiries. Management cautioned that enquiries will not all convert.
Management said it does not lose orders on price in international markets; competitiveness rests on reliability and service.
Commodity costs (copper, aluminium, steel) have risen; management said rate contracts and supplier diversification should protect margins, with some pass-through to customers after a time lag.
The NTPC CO2 battery storage project was taken at about 3% PBT margin; over two-thirds of it has been billed into revenue, and it is still marginally profitable after cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the near-doubled enquiry book is from existing versus new products and the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CO2 products are not in the enquiry book; the growth is steam-turbine based. North America enquiries rose about 1,000% from a low base, and the product enquiry book of about 18 GW is nearly double FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution of new initiatives (geothermal, MVR, CO2, drive turbines) and their FY26 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have a breakup; none is meaningful in the enquiry book yet. Geothermal and ORC are expected to be large over 3-4 years, MVR and heat pumps to stay small but high-margin, and drive turbines are cyclical with thermal power and oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: Why did export order inflow stay flat, and what is the conversion outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said geopolitical issues delayed finalisations, so enquiries did not convert; it expects better conversion in FY27 and exports above domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a number for FY27 order growth or double-digit revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined explicit guidance but pointed to about 9% closing order book growth as the minimum indicator for FY27 execution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin trajectory bottomed out, and what is the sustainable order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are stable on a YoY basis and vary with mix; a 25%+ EBITDA level is the reference. Order inflow is lumpy, and management aspires to a quarterly level above ₹500-700 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the NTPC strategic order and its margin?
qa_highlights.answer: The order is at about 3% PBT margin after cost increases, with over two-thirds already recognised as revenue.

risks_watch: Receivables of ₹6.39 bn (84 days) need to unwind in Q1-Q2 FY27; management expects receivables at March 2027 may remain at similar levels.
Rupee volatility mark-to-market losses (over ₹8.5 crore in Q4) may recur each year under the hedging policy.
Conversion of US and data-centre enquiries is slow because of water permitting, and the US subsidiary is still loss-making in FY26.
Export order conversion was flat in FY26 because of delayed finalisations; the Middle East conflict has delayed API orders.
CO2 energy storage project is still being validated, and its Indian costing and round-trip efficiency are unproven.
Commodity cost increases could compress margins if pass-through is delayed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and enquiry pipeline but cautious on timing: management repeatedly warned that conversion, the US ramp and FY27 execution will be back-ended, and it declined to give numeric guidance. It was defensive on the Q4 margin dip, attributing it to mix, the NTPC order and mark-to-market losses.

growth.why: Management declined explicit revenue guidance, pointing to ~9% closing order book growth as a minimum indicator for FY27, backed by a ₹20.54 bn order book (+8%), record Q4 export orders (+174%) and an enquiry book of ~18 GW that nearly doubled; no new capacity additions were disclosed and FY27 is back-ended.
